correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), \(k=g-n\) and \(n^2\equiv1\pmod g\). The exact two-ended carry equations constrain \(h=v-L\) to \(0\le h\le n\). The congruence uniquely determines the next outer digit; carry bounds force \(h=0,1\) for four states and \(h=n-1,n\) for the remaining four states. Substitution gives 16 table edges, the unique initial edge, reachability, and pivot classes. At \(n=3\), \((g,k)=(8,5)\), so the uniform graph identification proves the claimed isomorphism for every parameter; exact transition enumeration for \(3\le n\le60\) corroborates the algebra.

Holt shifted-symmetric criterion requires \(\gcd(g-k,k^2-1)\ge k+1\); here \(g-k=n\) and \(\gcd(g-k,k^2-1)=n<k+1\).

originality.rationale: Conjecture 3 of Kendrick (arXiv:1410.0106) states precisely the quadratic-family Young-graph isomorphism and provides no proof. Sloane (arXiv:1307.0453) constructs Y(8,5) and its count but not this family. Holt (arXiv:1410.2356) treats carry symmetry classes rather than these eight directed transitions. No equivalent/stronger covering result was identified in the actual targeted searches; remaining unlocated-literature risk is acknowledged. Holt (arXiv:1412.0231) Section 7.1 discusses derived graph-class examples including the reference class but does not imply the uniform quadratic parameter isomorphism.
residual_risks: A later or uncatalogued equivalent proof could have resolved Kendrick Conjecture 3; neither result search nor publication search establishes uniqueness.
Other related palintiple literature outside the three inspected full texts was not exhaustively surveyed.
Graph isomorphism is unlabeled; numerical edge labels are not preserved across base changes.
